extracted.intended_audience: KIPO examiners, patent applicants, agents (patent attorneys), and administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, standards and required contents for classifying, handling, examining, managing confidential (national defense-related) patent applications and for decisions on patent-term extension registration due to delay. Focused on Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) practice and interactions with the Defense Acquisition Program Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in decision to register or reject registration for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether to register patent term extension due to a delay in registration, the examiner shall write a decision to register extension or a decision to reject registration for extension indicating the following items and sign and seal such decision. However, a decision to reject registration for extension shall not contain the items ③ and ④ below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ① Application Number of Registration of Extension; ② Patent Number; ③ Period for Extension; ④ Content of Period of Delay; ⑤ Name and Address of Applicant of Registration for Extension (Title and Business Address in case of legal entity); ⑥ In presence of representative of applicant of registration for extension, Name and Address or Business Address of Representative (Title, Business Address and Name of Designated Patent Attorney where a representative is a patent law firm); ⑦ Order and Ground for Decision; ⑧ Date of Decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of determination on registration for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where registration for extension of the term of a patent right due to a delay in registration is determined, the Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office shall serve a certified copy of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details related to transmittal of a decision shall be referred to provisions regarding transmittal of a certified copy of a decision to grant/reject a patent right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements when extension registration is determined
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner determines registration of extension of the term of a patent right due to a delay in registration, he/she shall request the Registration Division to publish specified bibliographic items on the patent gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items to publish: ① the name and address of a patent right holder (the title and business address in case of a legal entity), ② the patent number, ③ the date of registration for extension, ④ the period for extension on the patent gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal period for decision to reject registration for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant who has received a decision to reject patent term extension may appeal the decision by submitting a notice of appeal trial to the decision to reject registration for extension within a statutory time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must submit the notice of appeal trial within thirty days from the date of transmittal of a certified copy of the concerned decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidation trial available for patent right registered for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent right whose term is extended falls under any paragraph of Article 134-2 of the Patent Act since the application to register patent term extension is determined for registration of extension, an applicant can request a trial to invalidate the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard invalidation trial procedures apply per the Patent Act (applicant may request invalidation where statutory grounds exist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government powers under Article 41 (national defense)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government may prohibit filing a patent application with a foreign patent office or may order an inventor, applicant, or agent to keep an invention confidential if necessary for national defense; may refuse to grant a patent or expropriate the entitlement to a patent during emergencies; and must pay reasonable compensation for losses incurred by such measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violating an order to prohibit filing abroad or to keep confidential results in being deemed to relinquish entitlement to a patent and to compensation rights. Procedures for prohibition, expropriation and compensation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of classification criteria (Article 11 Enforcement Decree)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of the Korean Intellectual Property Office shall determine the classification criteria necessary for selection of inventions to be treated as confidential under Article 41 after consulting with the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification criteria are set out in KIPO Directive No.651 (Classification Criteria of Patent Application Related to National Defense) and in an annexed form listing relevant IPC/CPC codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for confidential treatment referral to Defense Acquisition Program Administration (Article 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent application filed by a person domiciled or doing business in Korea conforms to the classification criteria, the Commissioner of KIPO shall refer the application to the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration to determine whether it should be classified and treated as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon reference, KIPO must notify the inventor/applicant/agent of the referral and request them to maintain confidentiality pending decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: DAPA reply timeline for confidentiality consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a referral from KIPO, the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration shall reply within two months whether the application needs to be classified and treated as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DAPA requests classification, KIPO shall take necessary measures in conformity with confidential service rules and issue orders to the inventor/applicant/agent to observe confidentiality; otherwise KIPO shall notify cancellation of the request for confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures and orders following DAPA request for confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a request to classify and treat any patent application as confidential, the Commissioner of KIPO shall take necessary measures in conformity with confidential service rules and order the inventor/applicant/agent to classify and treat it as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not requested, KIPO shall notify the inventor/applicant/agent of cancellation of the request for maintenance of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic consultation on cancellation/extension/change of confidentiality level (Article 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to patent applications ordered to be confidential, the Commissioner of KIPO shall consult twice or more each year with the Commissioner of the Defense Acquisition Program Administration regarding cancellation of confidentiality, extension of confidential period, or changes to the confidentiality level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ongoing management obligation to review the need for continued confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant right to request release, change, publication or licensing of confidential application
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor/applicant/agent who is ordered to classify and treat a patent application as confidential may request KIPO to release it from confidential treatment, to change the confidential level, or to publish or license the invention within specified limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such requests are subject to consideration under the applicable enforcement rules and may be granted or denied according to national defense needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two principal types of national defense-related applications and initial handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to national defense are divided into two types: (a) those filed with the applicant's indication that they are national defense-related, and (b) those classified as such by the examiner (including certain international applications flagged by IPC/CPC codes). Handling differs depending on type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant indicates at filing, the receiving division keeps the application secret, transmits a copy to DAPA, asks applicant/agent to keep it secret, and transfers to Patent Examination Policy Division for classification. If examiner classifies, examiner follows internal reporting and consultation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IPC/CPC classification codes to identify national defense-related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: KIPO maintains an annexed classification standard (Directive No.822) that lists IPC/CPC codes whose subject matter is considered national defense-related (e.g., specific codes for submarines, explosives, weapons, fuzes, rockets, armour, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Korea Institute of Patent Information assigns such a code, examiners are notified; in principle the application should be treated as national defense-related unless grounds for exception apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications eligible for national defense classification (including utility models and international applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications, utility model applications (mutatis mutandis), and certain international (PCT) applications that fall under the classification standard are eligible to be classified as national defense-related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications, transmittal of record and search copies to WIPO/ISA shall be withheld and documents transferred to the competent examination division when classification applies (per PCT Article 27(8)). See Security Operational Rule Article 78-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling mode: written proceedings vs online filing for national defense cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, proceedings for national defense-related applications shall be taken in writing. However, if an applicant is unaware the application is national-defense-related the applicant may file online; in that case an examiner can classify and specially manage the application as national defense-related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most national defense-related applications are submitted in writing (e.g., by defense institutes) with an explicit indication; but electronic filings may be converted to confidential handling as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant files indicating national defense at time of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: When an applicant files a national defense-related application in writing, the receiving division shall keep the application secret for security reasons, transmit a copy to DAPA for assessment, and request inventor/applicant/representative to keep the application secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If DAPA requests confidentiality, the division undertakes security measures, enters only bibliographic data electronically and transfers the application to the Patent Examination Policy Division for classification and then to the examiner in charge. If confidentiality is not required, the division lifts the confidentiality order and proceeds with ordinary handling, notifying the applicant/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for electronic filings later notified as national defense-related before transfer to examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application was filed electronically without indication but the applicant notifies it relates to national defense before transfer to the examination division, the application documents shall be printed confidentially and the electronic documents deleted from PatentNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director of the Information Management Division prints original, copy and one floppy copy and transfers them confidentially to the Application Service Division; standard handling for applicant-indicated national defense applications then applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review criteria and grounds for exception to national defense classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigning an IPC/CPC classification code that corresponds to national defense codes, the examiner shall determine whether to treat the application as national defense-related. In principle such applications need to be treated as national defense-related, but exceptions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for exception include: applicant has no address or business in the Republic of Korea; application does not fall under major defense materials specified in the Defense Acquisition Program Act; subject not among weapons systems specified in enforcement decrees; prior art identical or similar has already been disclosed; claimed invention is not related to national security/military secrets; application was incorrectly classified initially but was laid open to public before change. If difficult to determine, the examiner may consult the Director of the Emergency Affairs Subsection, the applicant, or a military expert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and decision flow when examiner identifies confidentiality need
rubrics_metrics.description: If during examination the examiner finds the application needs to be classified as national defense-related and no exemption applies, the examiner shall change the IPC code to the national defense code, proceed with confidentiality procedures, and report the intention to the director of the Patent Examination Policy Division with Annexed Form 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director of the Patent Examination Policy Division will then determine whether the application meets requirements to be classified as national defense-related; if so, further confidentiality handling and printing/deletion steps follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation-on-confidentiality handling steps (printing, deletion, transfer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a determination that an application may be confidential, the director of Patent Examination Policy Division requests the Information Management Division to print out and delete the electronic file, then confidentially handle originals and forward a copy to DAPA to confirm need for confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director shall also request inventor/applicant/representative to observe confidentiality under Article 12(2). If DAPA requests confidentiality, examiner keeps application secret per Administrative Instructions and transfers it to the concerned examination bureau; if not, the confidentiality order is lifted and the file is restored to the electronic system for ordinary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for confidential applications transferred to examination bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure for examining a confidential application is the same as that for an ordinary application, but examiners must be extra cautious to maintain confidentiality when borrowing confidential application documents from the examination bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After determining patentability, if the examiner decides to grant a patent the final confidential application documents (including amendments and written arguments) are sent to the Patent Examination Policy Division; if rejecting, final documents are sent to the Information Management Division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management and storage rules for confidential application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Divisions managing confidential documents and examiners shall carefully maintain confidentiality according to detailed rules: periodic consultation, notification obligations, withholding publication, record-keeping and secure storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules include: (①) consult with DAPA more than twice a year on cancelling/extending/changing confidentiality; (②) notify grant/registration in writing to Registration Service and Information Management Division; (③) withhold confidential applications from laying-open/publication until confidentiality lifted; (④) consult DAPA if technical contents no longer need secrecy; (⑤) conduct notifications/approvals/transmittals in secret and in writing; (⑥) keep registration documents with Patent Examination Policy Division until confidentiality order lifted; (⑦) amendments and written arguments of confidential applications shall not be assigned management numbers and shall be filed together as original and copy; (⑧) keep a copy of a confidential document with an assigned management number apart from the original; (⑨) observe Administrative Instructions Article 81 and Confidential Storage and Management rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical security and controlled access for confidential files
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential applications cannot be stored together with ordinary patent applications and must be kept in secure containers and registers; management responsibility is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential documents shall be kept in a double-layered steel container and the director of the Patent Examination Policy Division is primarily responsible; confidential applications shall be kept in a confidentiality register with management numbers noted in the margin of the patent register; confidential files can be lent only by writing on the confidential check-out list and an authorized person cannot be allowed for check-out except per the rules referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on filing confidential applications overseas
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 41, inventions crucial for national defense may be banned from filing overseas; such applications can be filed abroad only with government permission. Filing abroad in violation is deemed abandonment of entitlement to a patent and triggers liability for reasonable compensation for losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications subject to the ban include those classified by KIPO as confidential, indicated by applicant as national defense-related, or deemed necessary to keep confidential after consultation with DAPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and procedures for permission to file overseas (United States example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Korean government grants permission to file a banned application overseas (currently limited to the United States by bilateral agreement), permission is issued in writing after consultation with DAPA and subject to specified conditions and procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions include: (1) the specification content shall be clear and specific enough to examine the application in the United States; (2) the right to claim damages caused by confidentiality in the United States shall be waived except for damages due to use/disclosure by the United States without permission. Procedural steps: submit written request Form No.21; if permission granted, applicant must attach two copies of application documents, copy of permission, copy of representative's personal info and security clearance to the US application and submit those documents to DAPA; designate a representative who holds US security clearance; immediately notify DAPA of the US application number and filing date. The bilateral agreement limits filing to Korea and the United States under the confidentiality agreement.
